Examples of application to the case of trellis-coded modulation (TCM) schemes employing a 3*3 PSK signal constellation are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Symbolic two and three dimensional picture retrieval
abstract: Image retrieval using 2-D string matching techniques and pairwise spatial relationships is reviewed. It is demonstrated that 2-D string matching techniques can be extended to three or more dimensions and could form the basis of query systems to retrieve data such as CAD information. Algorithms are developed for 3-D type 0, 1, and 2 matching, and an example is presented. The three matching types provide progressively more exacting matches ranging from objects presence to exact submodel match. The query system based on pairwise spatial relations is extended to describe 3-D information.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The integrated services digital network (ISDN): economic and policy issues
abstract: Some fundamental policy issues that will influence the rate and direction of implementation of ISDN within a changing national and global telecommunication environment are examined. Additional criteria that ISDN must satisfy before it becomes a proven technology are indicated, together with additional constraints and potential problems. It is argued that if those involved in the technical design of ISDN are fully aware of telecommunication policy objectives, the technical design lf ISDN may be able to evolve in directions that will both improve the future of ISDN and assist in meeting policy objectives more effectively.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technology development for the flexible automation of fish processing
abstract: The seed activity of the research described in this paper has been the development of appropriate technology for flexible automation of the fish processing industry. Under the general theme of integrating advanced control techniques, high-level machine vision, and robotic devices, research is being conducted in all three areas, and a fish processing workcell is being developed. The problem of flexible automation of fish processing is introduced, and the appropriate use of control, machine vision, and robotics in this application is discussed. A workcell has been developed for the head removal operation of salmon. Particular emphasis is given to the problem of actuator selection, workcell integration, and the development of a hierarchical system for performance evaluation and control of the fish processing workcell.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A quantitative measurement for different testing methodologies
abstract: Theoretical basis for quantitative analysis within different software testing methodologies is discussed. A quantitative analysis to measure the difference between the All-P-USES criterion and the All-EDGES criterion used in program testing is described. Standards for the selection of test criteria are proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new asynchronous protocol for microcomputer communication
abstract: A new asynchronous protocol has been developed to meet the needs of microcomputer communication. The heart of this protocol is the 'break' signal, a unique signal that cannot be introduced in the standard data stream. Every standard command is preceded by the break signal. The command format contains the protocol signature followed by slave address, command bytes, I/O device address, the address from which data must be retrieved, and the number of bytes/sectors to be transferred. There are five different protocols defined for this asynchronous communication: bus arbitration protocol (BAP); command transfer protocol (CTP); bus access protocol (BACP); data transfer/receive protocol; and retransmission protocol.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: B-ISDN and the evolution of MAN
abstract: Evolutionary scenarios for metropolitan area networks (MANs) are described. They are compatible with, and complementary to, to the early expected forms of the broadband integrated services digital network (B-ISDN) and the third generation of local area networks (LANs). All use the asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) of operation. In this context, the MAN is seen as a distributor/concentrator switch operating on customer premises and in the periphery of the B-ISDN.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Powers and functions of Austel under the Telecommunications Act 1991
abstract: The functions and powers given to the Australian Telecommunication Authority (Austel) by the Telecommunications Act 1991 (the Act) are outlined. The functions, powers and directives are stated in the broad context of the Act, and two specific functions, the promotion of competition and consumer protection, are analyzed in more depth. In order to place these functions and powers in the wider legal context, the legal and administrative appeal procedures from an Austel determination pursuant to its powers and the principles of administrative law with apply are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impact of architecture choices on DSP circuits
abstract: Selection of proper architecture and implementation styles can strongly influence the performance of dedicated VLSI DSP circuits. The impact of architecture choices is illustrated by considering a number of representative signal processing examples and a few general architecture transformation techniques. It is shown that algorithm transformation techniques such as look-ahead computation can create concurrency in nonconcurrent recursive signal processing algorithms, and that inherently new signal processing algorithms are processed with concurrency. This leads to pipelined algorithm topologies without any hardware overhead. To illustrate the impact of the implementation styles, it is shown that the internal redundant number system can lead to more efficient realization of multipliers and adders. Using systematic folding and unfolding techniques, digit-serial architectures with no restrictions on the digit size can be described. All of these architectural techniques can increase the performance of DSP circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distributed computing at the European laboratory for particle physics
abstract: CERN, the European laboratory for particle physics, operates experimental facilities generating terabytes per year of data for 6000 particle physicists. CERN's history of involvement in local and wide area distributed computing is reviewed, and its response to the increasing impact of networked reduced instruction set computer (RISC systems while maintaining high quality services is discussed. These services include a program library, a distributed file, and tape management system, centrally operated RISC) services, data dissemination by satellite, and a distributed hypertext information system. The likely impact of an emerging integrated approach to distributed data analysis for particle physics on the future use of mainframe computers in the discipline is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: TENCON '92. 'Technology Enabling Tomorrow' 1992 IEEE Region 10 International Conference. Computers, Communications and Automation towards the 21st Century (Cat. No.92CH3223-5)
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Force controlled surface following without stability problems
abstract: The tracking of an unknown surface with a sensor controlled robot is used in sheep shearing robotics. There are intrinsic control stability problems associated with such sensor controlled robots when they are used in this way. These stability problems can be overcome by combining an active and passive control method and using an open loop force control. Specific issues addressed include the bandwidth problem, position control and the use of a hybrid follower.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error extension in decoding of line signal
abstract: The problem of propagation and multiplication of transmission errors during the decoding of a line baseband signal is discussed. General formulas describing an average number of data errors caused by a single transmission error (EREX), as well as a simplified one for optical fiber transmission systems, are given. Examples of EREX computation for different line codes utilized in optical fiber transmission systems, together with suggestions of possible applications of the formula, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The main field approximation to the cellular automata of nerve growth
abstract: The main field approximation in statistical physics is used to study the phase transition of the cellular automata (CA) dynamic with the noise factor. The CA are simulated in a majority vote model. Under specific conditions, it is shown that there may or may not be CA phase transitions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The impact of emerging technologies on military radio communications
abstract: A number of emerging radio communication technologies which promise to enhance contemporary military radio communications capability significantly are examined. Networking is seen as a mechanism for achieving greater connectivity, availability, and reliability in a tactical environment. Developments are reported, such as fast parameter estimation, adaptive link control, and network quality of service negotiation, which together indicate that such networks are potentially viable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new ordering method for FIR filters based on finite word length effect on moments of impulse response
abstract: The effect of the finite word length on the moment of the impulse response of a digital filter is investigated. It is shown that the quantization error in the moment values is almost linear with a slope of 3 dB/b and is well related to the output roundoff noise. An algorithm is also proposed to order the cascade sections of a finite impulse response (FIR) filter with low output roundoff noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fuzzy control of wing rock for slender delta wings
abstract: Fuzzy logic-based roll controllers are designed to control wing-rock motion of a free-to-roll stinged delta wing. The dynamics of an aircraft is a complex function of flight conditions. The free-to-roll stinged delta wing permits investigation of these variations, as well as the highly nonlinear dynamics of limit cycle at high angle-of-attack. A rule-base fuzzy logic control (FLC) is designed to suppress wing rock phenomena. The goal is to demonstrate the ability of FLC to capture qualitative control strategies and implement highly flexible control behaviors. A database FLC design method is used to improve performance characteristics to a level compatible with the performance of an optimal linear controller while maintaining high performance throughout the whole flight envelope.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development and testing of the trader for the RHODOS system
abstract: It is demonstrated that the design of a naming facility for the RHODOS system, which provides the maximum possible autonomy and flexibility to users yet at the same time allows them to share all accessible objects, is feasible. It is shown that autonomy and sharing can be achieved if: (1) two groups of sharable objects are distinguished (those which are owned by the system and those which are owned by each individual user); (2) these groups of objects form separate system and user domains; and (3) the possibility of exporting and importing objects to/from other domains is introduced. The latter allows users to access imported objects which are not available in their private domains.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Personal communications networking architecture and functionality evolution
abstract: The evolving personal communications network (PCN) will support services beyond mobile cellular telephony through the availability of personal communications terminals, which can be used in the home, in the office, or elsewhere. The universal personal telecommunications (UPT) service, an application of PCN, extends the association between the subscriber and the network by giving each subscriber a personal telecommunications number (PTN), which uniquely identifies a UPT subscriber. An overview of PCN architectures, PCN applications, and functionality evolution is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge acquisition in communication networks: towards flexible network management
abstract: The technology of very large knowledge databases (VLKDs) is employed in the network management system. An application which explores the knowledge acquisition from very large databases (VLDBs) in cooperation with a rule-based expert system for achieving flexible network management of interconnecting communication networks is investigated. The possibilities for the topology reconfigurations of networks as well as the optimal assignment of facilities in the network are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fourier analysis of MC/DPCM/DCT coded full-motion pictures
abstract: 2-D Fourier analyses are presented of coded video sequences using block matching motion compensation, intraframe and interframe discrete cosine transform (DCT) coding algorithms. In intraframe and interframe DCT coding, MPEG intraframe and interframe quantization matrices are employed as well as other variations. By examining the Fourier spectra of reconstructed video images, compared with those of the originals, different error patterns are identified and presented in the Fourier domain. The Fourier analysis also helps in searching for methods to improve coded video picture quality and alternative video coding algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Leadership for process improvement for reengineering success
abstract: The author reports on AT&T's total quality approach which defines an active role for senior management. The Process Quality Management Improvement (PQMI) methodology is outlined, symptoms of dysfunctional processes are summarized, leadership responsibilities are enumerated, human resource policy and goals are indicated, and suggestions for forming key business process teams are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Teleview server (public videotext)
abstract: Teleview is a public videotext service system designed to access a wide range of information and computer services. There is no platform to support access of Teleview in a network environment. The Teleview Server is one possible solution to bring Teleview to a network platform. An overview of the design and implementation of the Teleview server is given. The server allows several terminals on a LAN to share the same access line. The design can be ported to other networks such as ISDN. The limitation of the server is the speed in receiving page frames.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A VLSI architecture for salt-and-pepper filtering of classified images at video rates
abstract: An algorithm and VLSI architecture are described for salt-and-pepper filtering classified images. Small regions are reclassified to the mode of the class values in an n*n neighborhood window. An architecture has been developed that is scalable to neighborhood windows of reasonable size and still operates at video rates. The system contains multiple pipeline stages and incorporates a novel pipeline for computing the cumulative frequencies used to find the mode. The architecture has been simulated at both the functional and the transistor level to verify algorithm performance and obtain speed and area estimates. The filter will fit onto a 7*7 mm die using a 2 mu CMOS process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent DBMS for integrating alphanumeric and media data
abstract: The integration of preexisting alphanumeric data and media-data-like images, sound, and graphics generally results in a multidatabase system architecture. One can embed the media data into the alphanumeric part or regard alphanumeric and media data as equally important. It is demonstrated how the DEMOM (Description Based Media Object Data Model) can be applied to both approaches. DEMOM provides a uniform framework for managing different types of media data, enhanced with natural language content descriptions. In DEMOM media objects are defined as a class hierarchy of objects. The content descriptions form the basis for the creation of content/context hierarchies to support different organizations of media objects and are used for intelligent retrieval.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Upper limit estimation on the conversion gain of a mixer
abstract: A simple method for estimating the theoretical limit on conversion gain of an active device operating as a mixer is presented. The analysis is based on two sets of small-signal S-parameters measured at different bias conditions. This analysis applies to both FETs and bipolar junction transistors (BJTs) in emitter(source)-injected or base(gate)-injected configuration. This information is particularly useful in receiver design where the gain of a mixer is always an unknown or difficult to predict in the design stage, and can be used as a figure of merit in comparing the mixing performances of different transistors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of MIS using neural nets
abstract: An artificial neural network is useful for modeling enzyme release and estimation of myocardial infarction size (MIS). The backpropagation technique is used for adjusting the weights of the network with a measured enzyme activity in blood serum together with histologic value of infarction size (HIS). Once the weights of the interlayer connections are fixed, the network is used to estimate the MIS for unknown cases. With a proper choice of nonlinear function, the results are excellent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a distributed programming platform for parallel computation in a network of workstations
abstract: A programming platform that can gain the processing power of a network of idle workstations for distributed processing is presented. It allows users in a workstation to develop and execute distributed applications. Job scheduling is automatically performed. With this platform, users can make use of a simple parallel programming model to develop a parallel program and run it in a network of workstations. This platform eliminates low-level programming tasks such as process synchronization, protocol handling and error recovery.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A software-implemented baseband processor for digital communications
abstract: A digital multiplexer for low-speed synchronous data communications in a military environment is described. A 16-b embedded microprocessor is employed as a platform for executing real-time software to process the digital data signals. The system undertakes the clock recovery, plesiochronous buffering and data multiplexing for thirty low-speed data inputs. The implementation of a simple clock recovery algorithm is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Pole assignment for uncertain dynamic systems
abstract: Robust pole-placement for linear time invariant systems with structural uncertainty is discussed. It is shown that, upon the satisfaction of certain conditions, a linear time-invariant controller can always be found such that all of the closed-loop poles of the structurally uncertain system are placed in a prespecified region in the complex plane. A numerical example is given to illustrate the method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parameter estimation of multiple transient signals
abstract: A subspace decomposition and matrix pencil (SDMP) method is presented for temporal and spatial parameter estimation of multiple transient signals impinging on an array of sensors. The performance of SDMP methods is compared to that of the coherent signal-subspace processing method, where both methods are quantified. The estimation of the direction of arrival from a deterministic data model is studied, together with the use of the SDMP method on a totally wideband input.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SIMPAC: a simulator for parallel architectures and computing
abstract: An event-driven simulator for performance evaluation and modeling of parallel processing systems and parallel algorithms is presented. The system topology and architectural details are input to the simulator by means of a menu-driven graphics interface. The application program to be simulated is written in the metalanguage provided and mapped onto the system. The simulator produces performance metrics of resource utilization and process sojourns in various states. A trace file containing the log of the system, execution snapshots, and a module for graphical execution animation is provided for further analyses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New approach for over-the-cell channel routing
abstract: Obtaining small chip size is always an important goal in the automatic layout design of VLSI circuits. The advantages of using the routing area over the cells for interconnections to further reduce the channel width for the layout with standard cell design style is discussed. An efficient iterative algorithm for over-the-cell channel routing is presented. The execution speed of the router is significantly greater than that of previously reported units.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network approach to formant estimation
abstract: A neural network with two hidden layers is designed to estimate formant frequencies from linear predictive coding (LPC) coefficients. The formant estimation model reflects the nonlinear relationship between formants and LPC coefficients. Experiments of formant estimation on vowels and diphthongs are described and discussed. The results indicate that the neural network approach is a reliable formant estimation method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The intelligent test techniques of the electric machines
abstract: The electric machines measuring instrument is a specially designed system for intelligent testing of electric machines. It is fully automated. This system raises test efficiency and reduces labor hardship. The printed report of the performance of an electric machine using this intelligent test system is provided. The intelligent multifunction electric meter, the motor performance intelligent tester, the motor economical testing instrument, and the permanent magnet motor test are all described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of parallel processors
abstract: Techniques to evaluate the performance of user applications on parallel processors are reported. Intricacies caused by multiple job interactions and contentions on parallel processors are highlighted. It is important to consider the environment in which an application is to be run when predicting its performance. Towards this end, a methodology which is capable of predicting the performance of an application in real multi-user workloads has been developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new echo canceller with the estimation of flat delay
abstract: An echo canceller with flat delay estimation is described. It consists of flat delay estimation and a 64-tap echo canceller with time delay. The cross-correlation method is adopted to estimate the flat delay and the complexity of calculation is decreased for real-time processing according to the characteristics of the echo path. Simulation results indicate good performance in convergence rate and tracking capability for the time variant echo path. A block diagram of the hardware and a flowchart of the program are included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EDSIM-a Petri net simulator
abstract: A Petri net simulator is described. It is one of the tools developed in a project to produce a suite of well coordinated design tools with application in the design of complex, highly reliable digital systems. The simulator can be applied to a range of the most commonly used timed transition Petri nets. Features of the simulator such as the method it uses to resolve conflicts and the data structures which have been used to enhance its efficiency are described. Its performance is assessed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Differential phase shift keying modulation for WIN systems
abstract: Experimental results on indoor microwave data communication using differential phase shift keying (DPSK) to implement wireless in-building network (WIN) systems are presented. The unique characteristics of this wireless medium are reported, with emphasis on multipath problems and spasmodic links of the radio channel which distinguishes WIN from wired LAN media. Experiments measuring the bit error rate (BER) performance of the system in a laboratory are presented. 'Dead zones' in the laboratory are investigated by sending a pulse from an amplitude shift keying (ASK) transmitter and viewing the received signal on the ASK receiver. Feedforward automatic gain control, together with a simple antenna positioning topology, is proposed for implementation of the complete wireless LAN system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The numerical methods in non-contact measurements of deformations
abstract: The body of mathematics for noncontact measurements of deformation fields with the aid of a laser Doppler computer vibration meter is proposed. Continuous fields with given smoothness are restored on the laser experiment discrete fields using the extreme properties of spline functions. The algorithm has been implemented in order to find the portions of dangerous deformations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital neural network for the traffic control problem on crossbar switch networks
abstract: The traffic control problem on crossbar switch networks is represented by a parameter-free energy function. The proposed neural network is applied to update the state of the energy function until a stable state is reached. Within O(n) iteration steps, where n is the size of an n*n network, the energy function reaches a stable state which corresponds to a feasible solution of the traffic control problem. Simulation results show that this neural network also generates either optimal or near-optimal solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Observing the dominant state of linear dynamic systems
abstract: A reduced-order state observer design method based on model reduction is presented. The observer is able to asymptotically estimate the states of the dominant part of dynamical linear time-invariant systems. Conditions for asymptotic tracking of the states of the observed system are derived. A numerical example is given to illustrate the design method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a small scale PABX system using DSP technology
abstract: A flexible, low cost, and expandable digital private automatic branch exchange (PABX) system is developed. Digital switching and tone generation based on a digital signal processor are adopted. This reduces the overhead in assembling a small scale PABX system. The system can be expanded to handle more lines with the use of parallel processing techniques. A special software structure is developed to handle multiparty calls. The technique simplifies the programming of multiparty calls. Object-oriented design methodology is applied throughout the design of the call processing program. This results in a flexible program structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved error probability evaluation method for digital communication systems with applications to sequential decoding
abstract: It is often necessary to use Monte Carlo (MC) simulations for evaluating digital communication system performance in terms of bit error rates. The calculations of these error rates using a brute-force MC are difficult. An improved importance sampling (IS) technique for estimating the performance of coded communication systems which employ sequential decoders is presented. This technique uses an efficient simulation scheme for reducing the required number of simulation runs. Reduction is achieved by the use of 'biased' sampling distribution, which tends to increase the relative frequency of the rare error events.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convergence of recursive image restoration algorithms
abstract: Recursive image restoration is a powerful method for image restoration. Two-dimensional recursive filters usually require less computational time and storage requirements than nonrecursive algorithms and can handle space-variant blur easily. The convergent properties of a recursive algorithm, based on constrained deconvolution, are examined. Two versions of the algorithm are compared, and it is shown that a computationally fast version would be suitable for efficient practical image restoration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data-driven restoration of degraded binary MRF images using EM method
abstract: A data-driven restoration algorithm is developed for binary images degraded nonadditively with flip noises. The true image is assumed to be a realization of a Markov random field (MRF), and the nonadditive flip noises are assumed to be statistically independent and asymmetric. The parameter estimations of the noise and the true image are carried out iteratively in the context of an expectation and maximization (EM) procedure by approximating Baum's auxiliary function of the EM procedure. To approximate Baum's auxiliary function, the estimate of the true image at each EM iteration is used. Simulation examples show the effectiveness of the data-driven restoration algorithm and the parameter estimation procedures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An implementation of the entity-relationship model in type theory
abstract: The entity-relationship (ER) model has evolved from a database design tool to full-fledged database model. Existing prototypes of ER-based database systems use either relations or other record structures in the internal schema. Purely record based mappings are not adequate for supporting the rich semantics of the ER model in a natural way. The use of a rich and extensible type of system for the internal level representation of an ER database system is described. It is shown that the constructs of the ER model can be directly mapped to the internal level without loss of semantics. An algebra for data manipulation that has been implemented in a prototype of the ER database system based on a formal theory of types is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new graph-theoretic formulation for VLSI floorplan design
abstract: A new graph-theoretic formulation for floorplan design is introduced. The VLSI modules with their wire connections are represented as a weighted complete graph in which dummy edges are inserted between unconnected modules. The problem can be seen as one of extracting a maximal planar weighted subgraph from this graph. An operation referred to as the Gamma -operation is presented. It is used to develop an improvement procedure. The procedure is illustrated using an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new systolic algorithm for computing longest common subsequences
abstract: On the various algorithms proposed for the longest common subsequence (LCS) problem, systolic algorithms are the fastest. A new systolic algorithm that improves on previous systolic algorithms is presented. Compared with previous algorithms, it requires simpler operations as well as fewer I/O ports and data transfers between neighboring processing elements. The systolic algorithm requires fewer steps when recovering an LCS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Octree refinement using depth information for objects having concavities
abstract: All techniques for constructing 3-D models from a sequence of views have an inherent problem: if some parts of objects cannot be described by the edge of the projections, these parts of the objects will not be described by reconstructed 3-D models. A method to overcome this problem is presented by refining the octree models using depth images. In this method, an initial octree is constructed from a sequence of silhouettes. Depth images are captured from such viewing angles that the concavity information is sufficient. Each depth image is then converted into a sequence of binary images. Each binary image associates with the corresponding depth value. The octree is progressively refined by each binary image, based on examining the overlay of octree model, binary image, and depth value in 3-D space.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Competition in telecommunications-causes and consequences
abstract: The author presents a critique of the present structure of Australian telecommunications. He argues that certain specific questions were ignored in an attempt to rapidly introduce network competition in Australia. Among these are: the benefits derived from maintaining the Telecom monopoly; the reasons for and the consequences of the telecommunications reform in the UK, US, Japan, and New Zealand markets; and the impact of competition on development of the Australian network, the Australian equipment industry, and commercial broadcasting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Actively controlled mobility systems
abstract: The author discusses the coordination problem which arises in vehicles with large numbers of independently actuated joints designed to operate in unknown terrain. Coordination requires a considerable amount of sensor data. Some of this may be available from sensors required by other machine systems. Other necessary data mandates installation of sensor systems which would not otherwise be required. Much of the technology discussed is based on the adaptive suspension vehicle legged vehicle. An important application area for this technology is in planetary rover vehicles. A number of the diverse designs under study are reviewed with regard to their coordination requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and implementation of a knowledge base management system
abstract: A new data model and an approach for knowledge base management systems (KBMSs) are presented in order to integrate a relation model with term-rewriting techniques. An efficient KBMS has been designed and implemented with C and ORACLE, and has the following features: (1) multi-user-languages on the extensions of SQL, QBE, and PROLOG-like; (2) data/knowledge definition, representation and manipulation; (3) reasoning and explaining; (4) security and integrity check; and (5) optimal recursive processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fail safe node using transputers for railway signalling applications
abstract: A new fail-safe node using transputers for application in railway signaling systems is reported. This fail-safe node provides fault tolerance and safe reaction, which are required for railway signaling systems. The basic scheme of the fail-safe node is discussed, together with the concepts of leadership based on rotation, recovery in the fail-safe node, reconfiguration, and safe shutdown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvements on Fidge logical clocks
abstract: A logical clock mechanism has been developed for maintaining the partial ordering of events in distributed systems. The mechanism handles events in an ad hoc way and its comparison rule is not quite simple. Two major improvements on the mechanism are presented. General maintenance rules are developed to handle various kinds of interprocess events, and the comparison rule is simplified by maintaining the clocks with a new technique called two-phase update. These improvements make the logical clock mechanism more general and efficient for supporting distributed system development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evolution of an intelligent network
abstract: An intelligent network structure, its original technology, and the advanced services it can provide are described. The issues of traffic control, customized processing, multi-connection control and virtual network service control points (NSPs) are addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some legal issues raised by electronic trading
abstract: A discussion of the legality of electronic trading questions how electronic data interchange (EDI) systems accomplish the traditional legal goals of paper communication. These are: the display of proof that information is authentic; the communication of trade terms and conditions; the permanent storage of information; and the satisfaction of laws which require certain legal information to be 'written' and 'signed'. Other questions also emerge. How should trading partners and intermediary networks divide among themselves the risks of errors? How will Government record retention and control requirements be interpreted for electronic communication? What replaces the visible audit trail? Should the law be modified to clarify its applications to EDI?.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 200-1200 MHz CMOS techniques
abstract: Circuit and design techniques for high speed logic using standard CMOS processing have been developed. Several experimental chips performing real functions at speeds up to 1 GHz are demonstrated. Beyond normal speed improvement methods, two new methods are used. These are (1) a new clocking technique, the true single phase clock, and (2) transistor sizing using a new optimizer tool, SLOP (Switch Level Optimizer Program). Extensions of these methods are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experimental ATM network for B-ISDN research
abstract: An experimental asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) network for B-ISDN research is described. A novel architecture is employed in which the control processor for the switch is interfaced via an ATM link. It is suggested that this architecture offers a number of unique advantages over conventional switch designs for both network operators and manufacturers. These include flexibility in locating and dimensioning control processors and the opening of a new market in exchange controllers. The switch also features multiple discard and delay priority levels on a per VC/VP basis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reliability of symmetric hypernets
abstract: The reliability of a new multiprocessor interconnection network (symmetric hypernet) is determined and compared with the reliability of existing hypercube and hypernet structures. The reliability model is based on the clustering approach where a hypercube/hypernet of a higher dimension is first decomposed into smaller cubes until the reliability of the smallest cube is modeled exactly by means of the spanning tree approach. Clusters of these cubes are combined recursively until the reliability of the network under consideration is determined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An effective storage method during a sampling of speech signals
abstract: It is necessary for speech samples to be stored in a memory buffer before they are processed by speech analyzers without a real-time processor. An algorithm is proposed that uses the buffer efficiently when analog speech signals are converted to digital samples by the analog-to-digital converter. In order to implement this method in real time, the buffer is divided into the starting buffer and the remaining buffer. Until a voiced speech is found, the converted samples are sequentially stored in the starting buffer. The buffer is then shifted. When a voiced speech is found, the next samples are sequentially recorded in the remaining buffer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a neural network model for control in grasping a moving target
abstract: An approach to the control of a robot manipulator in grasping a simple moving target with constant speed is presented. A layered neural network architecture-based controller has been developed. It can automatically learn visual motor coordination for the fast reaching movements required in grasping a moving target. A learning scheme known as two-phase learning is described for teaching the skill to the controller. Learning in the controller is achieved through a sequence of trial movements without the presence of a 'teacher'. Visual feedback showing the action of the controller is used to adapt it so as to reduce the error between the target and the robot's gripper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple token bus protocol with priority
abstract: A simple token bus protocol with priority is proposed. The basic idea behind this new protocol is to pass the token to a station in the same (higher) priority class with a probability p/sub i/, and to a different (lower) priority class with probability less than p/sub i/. Results of a simple analysis for the case of no load show that the priority scheme is effective and the average walk time around the logical ring can be tailored to the priority of the station.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of high-speed slotted rings
abstract: A performance analysis of slotted rings is presented. The analysis is carried out under the same assumptions as those given for token rings, register insertion rings and register-insertion type slotted (RIS) rings. It is assumed that each node has a finite buffer space in order to calculate the probability of buffer overflow. This uniform set of assumptions makes it possible to compare the analytical results to each other. The analytical results are shown to be accurate by comparing them with simulation results. The performances of those protocols are compared in order to determine which is the most suitable protocol for a high-speed LAN environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Migration of ATM into the customer network
abstract: The likely nature of the traffic which future local area networks will handle is described. Such traffic will probably consist of two distinct classes: a delay sensitive class which will require stringent service qualities and will be controlled by means of connection admission; and a congestion sensitive class which will need to be flow-controlled. Two LAN paradigms are considered: LANs based on the use of shared media; and LANs based on the use of centralized asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) switches. It is shown that significant cost savings are likely to be achieved when LANs with high aggregate throughputs (greater than 1 Gb/s) are implemented using centralized ATM switches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A controlled study of the suitability and limitations of static modeling of speech
abstract: A static model (SM) in the form of a single vector is proposed to represent the temporal properties of a sequence of speech feature vectors. In contrast to a hidden Markov model which captures the conditional probabilities of state transitions of consecutive observations x/sub t/ and x/sub t+1/ over time, an SM captures their average joint probabilities of belonging to a pair of phonetic classes omega /sub i/ and omega /sub j/ without any Markovian assumption. An artificial vocabulary of ten words is designed to study the limitations of SM. Experimental results indicate that apart from a rather mild limitation of SM in handling certain types of vocabulary, SM performs better in terms of recognition rate as far as isolated word recognition is concerned.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the evaluation of a hybrid hypercube architecture employing data movement policies
abstract: Hypercube architecture can be modified for use in certain applications such as a knowledge base where shared data are used very often. A hybrid hypercube architecture in which a single copy of shared data is maintained is considered. The performance of such an architecture can be measured in terms of link cost and the communication cost. The performance measures of the proposed architecture are compared with that of hypercube architectures and that of some hypercube architectures with hierarchical interconnection networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Constant sidelobe pulse compression filter for periodic sequence
abstract: The design of a constant sidelobe compression filter for periodic sequences is presented. The response of the pulse compression filter to a periodic sequence is a central peak with constant sidelobe where the signal to noise ratio has been minimized. A design example, which demonstrates the performance of the filter for a periodic binary sequence with length 19, is given. If the loss in signal detectability is tolerable, the constant sidelobe approach enables the designer to make compromises between system sensitivity and the probability of detection error, and provides flexibility in the choice of usable code sequences.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Network management for integration of multi-purpose manufacturing laboratories
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirements of an integrated manufacturing engineering laboratory, a network of reduced instruction set computer (RISC) workstations and PCs is established. Apart from the general and advanced CAD/CAM applications, a wide variety of application software in manufacturing technology and real-time communication is supported. The installation of the network involves the use of UNIX TCP/IP on the high-end workstations and DOS Ver.5 with OS/2 LAN server and NetBIOS services. The problems encountered are discussed, in particular, the DOS network, set-up techniques, and management issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switching software reuse using object-oriented technologies and OODB
abstract: Reuse technologies for increasing the productivity of switching software development and for improving the software quality are described. Through analysis of switching systems, the most appropriate reuse method, the object-oriented method, is determined. To enhance reuse ability, an object-oriented database (OODB) for reusable switching software components is constructed. The OODB architecture and its features are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of an FDDI local area network with voice and data traffics
abstract: The performance of a fiber distributed data interface (FDDI) network with voice and data traffic is analyzed. A finite buffer is assumed at each station. In the analysis, voice traffic is modeled as an on-off model, and data traffic is modeled as a Poisson process. Through approximate analysis, the average queue length, the average waiting time, and the packet loss probability are derived. Simulation is used to examine the accuracy of the approximation. The effects of TTRT (target token rotation time) on various performance measures are investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of single sinusoidal likelihood functions using 2-D frequencies and polynomial coefficients as variables
abstract: The likelihood function can be parameterized with 2-D frequencies or their corresponding polynomial coefficients (frequency or polynomial likelihood function). It is found that the maximization of the likelihood function in the 2-D frequency domain is more computationally efficient than a previously proposed algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Organization of the CHISER Chinese sentence recognition system
abstract: A real-time Chinese sentence recognition system, CHISER, which consists of two parallel units (signal processing and symbolic processing) is described. The reasoning strategy presented, segmental left-to-right, can effectively control the backward propagation of errors in symbolic processing. Not only the whole sentence, but also any subsentences of an input sentence can be recognized. Experiments show that a 98% correct rate of sentence recognition is obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A recovery method for communication control processors
abstract: An efficient recovery method using checkpointing and journaling in communication control processors is presented. In the method, each process journals all received messages on stable storage together with indications of sending messages, and can recover its state independently by using them. Two ways of further reducing the recovery time are proposed: (1) establishment of checkpoints when the total amount of collected journals reaches a calculated value based on the recovery time requirements; and (2) execution in the recovery mode of the copy codes of a failed process in which message-input and output instructions have been modified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hypertext approach to enterprise modelling
abstract: The application of a hypertext authoring approach to enterprise modeling is considered. A hypertext transformation model for systems development is developed. This model views systems development as a transformation process. The role of hypertext in this process is in providing support for information capture, whereby nodes of information are created, and links made between them. The attachment of attribute/value pairs to the nodes and links makes flexible transformation and (re-)structuring of captured information possible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Scheme for secure digital mobile communications based on symmetric key cryptography
abstract: A scheme for secure digital mobile communications is proposed. The scheme requires the introduction of an online network center for session key distributions. Both user authentication as well as key distribution are automatically included. The scheme can also protect the system from the attacks of replay. Private-key algorithms are used for data encryption. The scheme can be implemented even in a hardware-limited terminal to achieve secure digital mobile communications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Robust model-following control
abstract: Model-following systems which minimize an H/sub infinity /-norm related to the tracking error are developed by solving an algebraic Riccati equation. In the presence of the plant parameter uncertainties, stability robustness and performance robustness are achieved using mu -synthesis. The robustness of the proposed designs is demonstrated in an example, and the results of linear-quadratic-Gaussian model-following control (LQC-MFC), H/sub infinity /-MFC, and robust-MFC are compared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Array processing of wide band signals with computation reduction in coherent and incoherent environment
abstract: A high resolution iterative algorithm for estimating the direction-of-arrival (DOA) of multiple wideband sources is proposed. For equally spaced array structures, two unitary transform based approaches are proposed in the frequency domain for signal subspace processing in both coherent multipath and incoherent environments. Given prior knowledge of the initial estimate of the DOA, with proper spatial prefiltering to separate multiple groups of closely spaced sources, the proposed algorithm is shown to have a high resolution capability even in coherent multipath environments without reducing the angular resolution as compared to the use of subarrays. The performance of the algorithm is demonstrated using simulated data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A remote computer based surveillance and control system for telecommunication equipment
abstract: A microprocessor based system provides 24-hour remote surveillance and control of telecommunication equipment. The system allows automatic manning without human intervention and the presence of manpower at the center. The design and development of the system are described. Real-time point-to-point digital communication between the telecommunication equipment and host computer presented is discussed. Hardware and software design techniques and experimental results are summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Efficient 2-D systolic array implementation of a prime factor DFT algorithm
abstract: A new two-dimensional systolic array for computing the discrete Fourier transform (DFT), with length N decomposable into the product of two relatively prime factors, 4M/sub 1/ and M/sub 2/, is presented. The architecture is constructed based on the row-column algorithm. It does not include any intermediate circuit for arranging data flow between the row-DFT and column-DFT modules. The system possesses the features of regularity and modularity, and is well suited to VLSI implementation. It has an efficiency of 100%, a throughput rate of one N-point transform per M/sub 2/ cycles, and an area*time/sup 2/ figure of AT/sup 2/=O((M/sub 1/+M/sub 2/)M/sub 2/N log/sub 2//sup 2/N), which is much smaller than the value of O(N/sup 3/ log/sub 2//sup 2/N) achieved by existing linear systolic array solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bit-string optimization in a brachytherapy dosimetry problem
abstract: A problem in radiotherapy planning is solved by applying the following search algorithms: artificial genetic search, with fixed crossover probability, with variable crossover probability, and with cut-point distribution; simulated annealing, serial and parallel; stochastic hill-climbing; next-ascent hill-climbing; and steepest-ascent hill-climbing. Given a number of points at each of which a predetermined dose of radiation is required, the problem is to optimize the settings of the radiation sources present in each of three directions (X, Y, and Z) in a three-dimensional selection device such that the sum-squared dose variation is minimized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mobile payphone system
abstract: The challenges confronted and overcome in the development and production of the mobile payphone system are reported. The main objective was to create a phone system that would present a Mobile Payphone Terminal (MPT) to the user that was easy to use, operationally sophisticated, flexible, highly reliable, compact and of low cost. To achieve this, several diverse existing technologies were incorporated. The systems approach utilized allows the synergy of the complementary remote payphone terminals and central management system to be achieved. This solution has permitted the development of an extremely flexible remote monitoring facility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new structure of parallel filter bank allowing perfect reconstruction
abstract: New parallel filter banks allowing perfect reconstruction which are categorized in coding intermediate between subband coding and predictive coding are presented. M-channel filter banks allowing perfect reconstruction are represented mathematically, and filter banks categorized in the above coding are discovered. Three types of three-channel filter banks are designed. The coding gains of these filter banks are then maximized, i.e., the filter coefficients are optimized from the viewpoint of energy compaction property. Computer simulation shows that the designed filter bank performs well.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Image coding using fuzzy vector quantizer
abstract: The fuzzy vector quantizer (FVQ) technique is applied to image coding when a square image subblock is mapped into a reproduction codeword. The FVQ is also tested on a database of Gauss Markov sources to demonstrate its performance in coding highly correlated data. An attempt is made to determine whether the use of softer decisions in the FVQ training step would optimize the codeword distribution and make the quantizer adapt well to random initial codebooks. The experiments show that FVQ coding performs better than standard methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Representing spatial knowledge in design
abstract: In interior design, there are some basic guidelines or rules to follow. A program, called 'Interior Design Expert' (IDX), is introduced. It is an intelligent CAD system for interior design. IDX goes beyond typical CAD systems. Using AI techniques, it analyzes a design, extracts relevant spatial relationships, applies high-level design rules to the resulting internal representation, and then generates intelligent design suggestions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A decentralised remote procedure call transaction manager
abstract: A model for decentralized management of remote procedure call (RPC) transactions in a distributed system is presented. After the introduction of the problem and the RPC transaction model, the algorithms and some properties of the transaction management model are described. The decentralized RPC transaction management model has no transaction coordinators and therefore can tolerate any host failure. The model is transparent to programmers. It can act as a run-time system within the programming environment. Programmers can use RPC transaction calls as usual RPC calls.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Relation between bit and symbol error probabilities for frequency shift keying with limiter-discriminator-integrator detection
abstract: In M-ary, Gray coded digital communication, the bit error probability is usually approximated by the symbol error probability divided by the number of bits in a symbol. This approximation is excellent for phase shift keying (PSK) with coherent detection at high-signal-to-noise ratios and Gaussian channel. The exact bit error probability for M-ary frequency shift keying (FSK) with limiter-discriminator-integrator detection in Gaussian, Rayleigh, and Rician channels is computed. The results are compared with the approximation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Customer adaptive communication services
abstract: A direction for the development of future customer adaptive communication services that seeks to deal with the complexity of these services by making them more adaptive to the individual user is presented. User modeling, the process of construction of computational models of users, is described. The promises of customer adaptive services are explored by means of two current research projects: a personal news reader and an audio tutorial for advanced telephony services. Personal information filtering which aims to reduce the volume of electronic form news information by establishing personal interest profiles based on user modeling is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Matrix pencil method for inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging
abstract: A study of a new high-resolution method called the matrix pencil method for inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging is presented. Simulation comparison of the matrix pencil method and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) method demonstrates the superiority of the matrix pencil method. The matrix pencil method is tested on a real data set and it is found to be very successful as compared to other high resolution techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Heterogeneous networking for computers and communications in broadband environment
abstract: The evolution of broadband networks through heterogeneous networking among the set of broadband networks that are being developed, i.e., broadband ISDN, (B-ISDN), fiber distributed data interface (FDDI) LAN, MAN, and distributed queue dual bus (DQDB), is considered. The evolution scenario based on business customer needs is stressed. The interworking requirements are outlined, and the strategies in developing heterogeneous networks to support computer communications through connectionless services and telecommunications through connection oriented (CO) services are proposed. A performance evaluation of the interworking unit (IWU) is presented. The delay characteristics of CO and connectionless (CL) services are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A floating point rectangular systolic array on a chip
abstract: The logical design and architecture of a floating point systolic array on a chip are described. The layout is presented, with a microphotograph of a functional chip fabricated in a 1 mu m CMOS process. The instruction set of the chip is described, and its application to matrix operations is discussed. The chip will function either in isolation or in a cascaded one- or two-dimensional array. In these latter configurations it will be possible to build processing nodes with computing rates in excess of 1 Gflops.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A processing method of class-2 unknown Japanese compound words of two components with use of in-word grammar and its prototype system implementation
abstract: Techniques of natural language processing are applied to many kinds of systems. But no systems have the ability to process unknown words. Especially in Japanese, it is essential for systems to have such abilities. A method using in-word context is proposed to process class-2 unknown Japanese compound words of two components. First, unknown Japanese words are classified into three classes. Then, in-word grammar for compound words of two components is organized to build a lexicon. A system is implemented to evaluate the proposed method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An emitter-injected mixer with improved conversion gain, efficiency
abstract: Traditional emitter-injected mixers use an inductor placed between the emitter and ground to produce voltage feedback to the transistor for mixing purpose. This configuration provides good port-isolation but low conversion gain due to the presence of the feedback impedance between emitter and ground which reduces the gain of the transistor. It is observed that by replacing the inductor with a diode and choosing suitable bias points for both the transistor and the diode, an improvement in the conversion gain of a few dB and a better collector efficiency can be achieved. The conversion gain of this kind of mixer is analytically predictable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Nucleus-microkernel for the RHODOS distributed operating system
abstract: New architectural approaches are required in the design of distributed operating systems, to meet the requirements of openness and high performance. One approach is to build the distributed operating system as a set of independent system servers, cooperating through a small set of primitive operations provided by a microkernel. The Nucleus is the microkernel of the RHODOS system. It is explained why a microkernel-based design was chosen. The features and advantages of the system are reported, and the Nucleus data structures and other services provided to facilitate the microkernel abstraction are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive training of artificial neural network
abstract: Adaptive training of a neural network for nonstationary processes is reported within the framework of a multilayer perceptron model using the backpropagation (BP) algorithm. The error introduced by small changes in system parameters is reflected to adapt the changes in the converged weight matrix. The error is minimized using a constrained optimization method like the gradient projection method (GPM). The method is applied for harmonic prediction in voltage waveforms. The results for a sample system are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: VSAT-based satellite wide area networks
abstract: The performance of very small aperture terminal (VSAT)-based satellite wide area networks is evaluated. VSATs are used as gateways to interconnect local area networks through satellites to form a wide area network. The delay of the network, which is the time needed to send a packet from a station in the source LAN to a station in the destination LAN, is analyzed. Several access protocols are considered for comparison. It is observed through numerical examples that time division multiple access (TDMA) on the uplink and time division multiplexing (TDM) broadcast on the downlink offer the best delay performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of a linear image processor
abstract: A linear array can be applied to both low-level and intermediate-level processing tasks. The design of a semi-single instruction, multiple data (SIMD) linear array for low-level processing tasks is described. Its special features include a dual-communication channel, a decoding network and a binary unit. Its potential applications in intermediate-level processing are also addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eliminating the numerical oscillations in the transient simulations of power systems using novel mathematical models
abstract: Two mathematical models of the electrical elements of power systems for digital simulations of transients are presented. These models can be used to eliminate numerical oscillations in the simulation calculations caused by the frequent changes of the topological structures of the networks. These models offer high precisions, and are convenient to use.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Response of parallel multi-impedance transmission line excited by plane wave
abstract: The terminal response of a transmission line with parallel multi-impedances excited by a plane wave is discussed. General computing formulas are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelligent networks
abstract: Intelligent network (IN) architecture increases the speed to market of services and features, while providing a greater level of customization. The basic concept and some early uses British Telecom has made of the approach are described. Likely future directions in the technology are also discussed. In intelligent networks, some elements of call processing are moved outside of the switch to an attached computing platform. This computer can then be programmed by the network operator to provide the new feature or service. This processor is called the Service Control Point (SCP). The Digital Derived Services Network (DDSN) which provides premium rate services within the British Telecom (BT) network is described, together with the BT-developed Cashless Services Network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive controller for marginally stable nonlinear systems using neural networks
abstract: A method for the adaptive control of a marginally stable discrete-time nonlinear system of unknown structure is presented. The method is based on the model reference control technique in which the output from the nonlinear plant is made to track the output of a stable reference model which reflects the desired dynamics. Multilayered neural networks are used to approximate the plane dynamics and to implement the controller. Simulation studies show that the proposed scheme performs well under different working environments. Various design parameters that have significant influence on the performance of the overall system are discussed. The effect of the learning rates is highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple machine (based on the SK-combinator reduction mechanism)
abstract: A simple machine architecture based on an extension to the combinator notation is described. Code travels along a unidirectional stream and is executed in parallel by simple finite state machine based cells separated by sections of a first-in, first-out (FIFO) buffer. The resulting regularity and structural simplicity ensure a good match to VLSI implementation. It is verified that the extended combinator is a viable execution model. Preliminary simulation results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Holographic implementation of mirror-folded free-space crossbars
abstract: It is shown that the canonical crossbar arrangement for free-space beams can be folded by means of two plane mirrors onto their plane of symmetry, thereby making it possible to place all the required 2*2 elements in that single plane or even on a single line. The holographic implementation of this reconfigurable 2*2 mirror-folded generalized crossbar with a thermoplastic holographic camera is reported. The bypass, exchange, and broadcast states are demonstrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Future network management
abstract: Current research and standards activities for future network management are discussed. Specific topics addressed include: management tasks; peer management systems; open distributed processing (ODP) and network management integration; the telecommunications management network (TMN) concept; integration using the TMN; layering; domains; and automated management.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The performance of trellis-coded modulation
abstract: Trellis-coded modulation (TCM) in an 8-PSK (phase shift keying) scheme is more power efficient than uncoded QPSK at the same spectral efficiency on perfect coherent detection. For the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of phase reference, the sensitivity to phase offset for 8-PSK is more serious than for uncoded QPSK. To analyze the effect of imperfect coherent detection, the equivalent distances under recovered carrier phase offsets are derived. The conditional event error probability and its upper bound with respect to recovered carrier phase offset are taken into account. The results for the average bit error probabilities of the 4-state, 2/3-TCM and uncoded QPSK schemes with noisy phase reference are given. It is shown that very high values of phase reference SNR are required for the efficient implementation of the TCM scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Symbolic and numerical investigation of manipulator performance limiting factors
abstract: The application of computer algebra and numerical simulation to investigate the dynamic performance limiting factors of a Puma 560 manipulator is discussed. Using simple computer algebra programs, it is possible to gain insight into the configuration-dependent dynamic terms and their effect on independent joint axis control strategies. The manipulator's base parameter set can be determined, and a form of the dynamic equations suitable for linear parameter identification can be generated, together with efficient run-time codes for computed-torque or feedforward control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dimensioning of both-way circuits with overflows to separate routes
abstract: An approximated method for the dimensioning of both-way circuits with different overflow routes is presented using the equivalent random method. Numerical examples are used to illustrate the effects of the volume and distribution of traffic, of the number of circuits on the overflow, and of the direct routes on the call congestion. The relation between call congestion and the number of circuits on the overflow route is given, while keeping the total traffic volume and the number of direct circuits constant for different sets of traffic distribution. The both-way circuit is compared with the single direction operation using the same traffic profile and distribution and the identical number of direct and overflow circuits. At an acceptable call congestion level, the both-way circuit outperforms single direction operation, in addition to improving circuit utilization and flexibility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided analysis, design and modeling of optical fibre receivers
abstract: For optical fiber transmission systems, the evaluation of the average error probability can be extremely difficult using analytically based methods because of the complex nature of the stochastic processes involved. An importance sampling method is presented for simulating optical fiber communications systems which employ avalanche photodetectors. The proposed method is a computationally efficient simulation-based tool for use in computer-aided-designed, analysis, and modeling of digital lightwave communication systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: NETPLAN-a telecommunications network planning support system
abstract: A software system, NETPLAN, for supporting telecommunications network planning has been developed. It is implemented using Prolog with a user-friendly graphical interface based on X Windows and Motif. The three basic activities of network planning (routing design, one-way and both-way junction circuit design, and signaling network design for circuit-switched networks) are fully supported. The dimensioning of the junction circuits is optimized by considering noncoincidental busy hour traffic characteristics of the various routes using the 24-hour traffic profile. The object-oriented approach adopted by NETPLAN eliminates the need for defining traffic and routing matrices as required by conventional approaches. The usefulness of the system is illustrated by its application to the planning of a network with ten switching nodes and twenty interconnected links.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recursive descent techniques for ASN.1 decoding and encoding
abstract: The design of Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) coders and compilers using recursive descent techniques from its theoretical basis in compiler theory to software engineering considerations is examined. LL(1) compiler theory is used to develop parser tables and state transition diagrams for recursive descent decoders. A generic decoder is developed which includes specific ANS.1 specification information in tables generated using YACC and LEX. The decoder requires small amounts of code and can be used for general ASN.1 syntax specifications without modification, making it suitable for rapid prototyping applications. The storage of data is achieved by means of lists rather than conventional programming structures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cyclic inheritance detection for object-oriented database
abstract: Inheritance is the main theme of schema design for the object-oriented software and object-oriented database. Misuse of inheritance will lead to cyclic inheritance which suffers from redundant classes and endless self-inheritance. For a class hierarchy with cyclic inheritance, to detect all the cyclic inheritances is a NP-complete problem. A graph-theoretical reduction methodology to reduce them in polynomial time is described. An algorithm to support this reduction is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
